cells.tense: Your persistence is steady here, and it does not need to be pushed.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Carry your own share the whole way through one thing, without handing it off or waiting for someone to lift it with you.
cells.core:
You have a way of keeping on with what you set out for that doesn't thin out when conditions turn. Where what you are shows itself, you can work without checking that you belong there, and that's most of why it holds. What runs through you is patient rather than loud. It is not being forced just now.

So carry your own share the whole way through one thing, this week. Not everything at once — one thing, all of it. You'll learn how much of your strength is yours when nobody else is lifting alongside. That is what steady looks like here. Not rest — just no extra weight to haul on top of the actual work.
cells.sheetLine: You carry your own share and it holds.
cells.verb: keeping on with the thing you set out for, after everything that has happened
cells.place: the place where what you are shows itself

cells.tense: You are braced for a next version of things that has not arrived, and you are living inside it already.
cells.act: hold two true things without declaring either
cells.ask: Take a place where you have your answer ready, and hold it a week without saying it — let both possibilities stay open, and watch what the waiting does.
cells.core:
Keeping on has tipped into keeping watch. Where what you are shows itself, you are standing in a version of things that hasn't happened yet — scanning for the turn, rehearsing your response before there's anything to respond to. The strength is real. Running it out in the future is what's tiring you.

You can afford to hold what you know longer before it hardens into a position. When you have your answer ready, hold it a week without saying it. Let both possibilities stay open. The pressure drops when you stop pre-living it. What was going to happen still happens — and you'll be here for it, not somewhere further on.
cells.sheetLine: You are living next week before it arrives.
cells.verb: keeping on with the thing you set out for, after everything that has happened
cells.place: the place where what you are shows itself

cells.tense: The door you're still standing at is behind you, and you haven't turned around.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Look after something you already have — a room, a body, a bill, a friendship — with a steady hand. Just that. Nothing else has to change for it to count.
cells.core:
Where what you are shows itself, you've stopped arriving. Something you finished or left is still holding your shape, and you are standing in it rather than in this week. The persistence hasn't gone anywhere. It's waiting for you to be present again so it has something to work on.

One small tending brings you back. Look after something you already have — a room, a body, a bill, a friendship — with a steady hand. It has no drama in it, which is exactly why it works. You'll find yourself in the week you're actually in, and the strength that was idling will have something to hold.
cells.sheetLine: You are still at a door that closed behind you.
cells.verb: keeping on with the thing you set out for, after everything that has happened
cells.place: the place where what you are shows itself

cells.tense: The persistence carrying you through is being filed under circumstance, and it belongs to you.
cells.act: persist on your own reserves through the pressure
cells.ask: Notice the next difficulty you meet and stay with it on your own reserves — no rescue, no waiting. Just those hours, carried by yourself.
cells.core:
You are on the other side of things that would have folded other people, and if someone said so you'd say there was no choice. That persistence isn't circumstance and it isn't accident. It's yours. Where what you are shows itself, the credit is sitting unclaimed, and only you can pick it up.

Notice the next difficulty you meet, and stay with it on your own reserves — no rescue, no waiting for anyone. Just those hours, carried by yourself. You don't have to feel proud of them. You only have to stop filing them under things that happened to you instead of things you did.
cells.sheetLine: The strength getting you through is filed under luck.
